x_comments.alpha_K: Capital share set to 0.33 (same as Germany) for cross-country comparability. PWT 11.0 labsh for Poland averages 0.59 (2000-2019), implying alpha=0.41, but this is likely inflated by transition-era measurement issues (volatile range 0.54-0.66). Using 0.33 also avoids excessive BGP K/Y that produces implausibly large Ramsey detrending residuals.
x_comments.delta_annual: 6% annual depreciation for total-economy capital. Higher than Germany (5%) to reflect faster capital obsolescence in post-transition Poland. Tested 6.5% and 7% but these depressed the trend too much (y corr dropped from 0.79 to 0.60). Combined with K/Y=2.7 override, 6% gives the best balance across Y, C, and investment detrending.
x_comments.beta_annual: Discount factor: 0.96 annual. Under the terminal-growth convergence calibration, the terminal modified-golden-rule BGP real rate is about 6.0% annual with g_A converging from 1.5% to 0.8%.
x_comments.sigma: Inverse IES (CRRA coefficient). sigma=1.5 is mid-range consensus (1=log, 2=high risk aversion).
x_comments.tfp_growth_annual: 1.5% annual TFP growth during the historical in-sample period. Poland is a catch-up economy with higher TFP growth than Germany (0.5%). The forward extension and terminal BGP instead use terminal_growth.g_A_terminal_annual = 0.8% to avoid imposing permanent catch-up growth.
x_comments.K_override: Override initial capital stock K_0 (million EUR, chain-linked 2015). PIM gives K/Y=2.0 (K=509k), PWT 11.0 cross-validates at K/Y=2.21. Setting K/Y=2.7 (K=688k) combined with delta=0.065 (BGP K/Y≈2.95) gives PIM/BGP≈0.92, close to Germany's ratio. Accounts for unmeasured housing/informal capital. Set to 0 to disable override and use PIM.
x_comments.phi: Inverse Frisch elasticity on extensive margin. Current Poland calibration is phi=1.35. This remains provisional and should be re-estimated from dedicated Polish SimPaths experiments when available.
x_comments.labor_supply: Default Ramsey labor-supply mode. calibrate_growth_model.m copies this template into simpaths_export and writes the calibrated runtime fields there.

base_year_values.WAP_comment: Working-age population (15-64), thousands. Source: World Bank SP.POP.1564.TO (UN WPP), Poland 2005. Must match build_population_projection.m age range.
base_year_values.x_comment: calibrate_growth_model.m writes calibrated base-year levels and derived fields into simpaths_export/Poland/growth_params_Poland.json.

inflation_target.x_comment: NBP (National Bank of Poland) inflation target is 2.5% (+/- 1pp). Differs from ECB 2% target used for Germany.

labor_trends.demographic_L_source: Eurostat population projections + GUS labor force participation
labor_trends.x_comment: NAWRU from AMECO (or OECD). L_demo from Eurostat/GUS. Hours: log-linear trend fitted to observed.

solver.x_comment: Stacked-time Newton (LBJ) perfect-foresight solver with terminal K/Y closure. The solve runs over the observed sample plus a terminal tail of 600 quarters (~150 years); Newton convergence requires ||F||_inf <= 1.0e-10 within 200 iterations.

terminal_growth.x_comment: In-sample detrending uses tfp_growth_annual = 1.5%; the forward extension converges quarter-by-quarter toward g_A_terminal_annual. 0.5% is the long-run anchor consistent with completion of EU income convergence (AMECO/AWG long-run productivity assumptions for converged member states), and is also chosen to align the Ramsey forward wage trend with the vanilla SimPaths wage trend (~1.5%/yr), enabling clean treatment-effect comparisons. rho_quarterly = 0.985 (~12yr half-life) speeds up convergence relative to the previous 0.99 (~17yr half-life).
